question: When I flatten a stage to ship a single USD file to third parties, the variant sets get resolved and only the selected variant remains. How can I flatten it and still keep the variant sets, so recipients can switch variants?
fact1: Flattening a stage (UsdStage::Export/Flatten, usdcat --flatten) evaluates variants and keeps only the opinions of the currently selected variants.
fact2: Flattening a layer stack (usdcat --flattenLayerStack or UsdUtilsFlattenLayerStack) combines the sublayers into a single layer while preserving all other composition arcs, so variant sets survive.
note: Layer-stack flattening keeps references/payloads as arcs, so external files are not baked in; the docs do not cover a full single-file flatten that keeps variants.

question: On the same prim, are collection-based material bindings stronger than direct bindings? In my experience direct bindings win, but the bound material resolution rules say collection-based bindings are stronger.
fact1: If a prim has a direct binding and is directly targeted by a collection binding, the direct binding wins by default.
fact2: The bindMaterialAs metadata (strongerThanDescendants) can make a collection-based binding override descendant prim bindings.
note: The UsdShade proposal (wp_usdshade.rst 148-153) states the opposite (direct weaker than collection on the same prim); the user guide reflects current behavior. Good conflicting-source probe.

question: If I only care about a primvar authored directly on the mesh, can I access it with GetAttribute("primvars:foo") like a normal attribute, or are there cases where I should go through UsdGeomPrimvarsAPI?

fact1: Primvars are accessible as attributes.
fact2: Indexed primvars keep their indices in a separate attribute (primvars:NAME:indices).
fact3: Blocking the primvar attribute directly blocks only the elements, not the indices; UsdGeom.PrimvarsAPI BlockPrimvar() blocks both.
note: The docs do not say whether plain Get/Set is otherwise equivalent; the blocking/indices caveat is the only stated difference.

question: In a prim spec's reference list, what is the difference between prepended and appended references, and why does AddReference() produce prepended references?

fact1: An appended item goes to the back of the resolved list, so an arc appended in a stronger layer is weaker than same-type arcs appended from weaker layers.
fact2: A prepended item goes to the front, so an arc prepended in a weaker layer is still stronger than same-type arcs appended from stronger layers.
fact3: The UsdReferences API creates prepended references by default so the reference contributes stronger opinions than references in weaker layers; the position parameter allows other options.
note: The legacy 'added' list op is not explained anywhere in the corpus.

fact2: With instancing you cannot uniquely override prims beneath the instance root.
fact3: Direct material bindings cannot be established for gprims inside instances without breaking the instances.

question: Is there a way to retime a layer or stage with a non-linear frame mapping (for example frame 50 to 100, frame 51 to 102), given that a layer offset only supports a constant offset and scale?
